text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive commutative group structure and a measurable-space structure satisfying BorelSpace. Write dx for volume measure on E. Let W : E → ℝ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, and assume that x ↦ exp(−W(x)) is integrable with respect to volume. Let μ be the tilted volume measure with potential −W, namely the measure obtained by normalizing the density exp(−W) relative to volume. Let D be any partial ℝ-linear map from L²(μ; ℝ) to L²(μ; E). Assume that D is closable, and assume the following exact characterization of its graph: for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E), the pair (u,G) lies in graph(D) if and only if there exists a smooth, compactly supported function f : E → ℝ such that the measurable representative of u equals f μ-almost everywhere and the measurable representative of G equals ∇f μ-almost everywhere. Here ∇f is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative of f. Then, for every u ∈ L²(μ; ℝ) and G ∈ L²(μ; E) with (u,G) ∈ graph(closure(D)), for every continuously Fréchet differentiable, compactly supported function φ : E → ℝ, and for every vector v ∈ E, both functions x ↦ φ(x)⟨G(x),v⟩ and x ↦ u(x)(dφ(x)[v] − φ(x)dW(x)[v]) are integrable with respect to μ, and ∫_E φ(x)⟨G(x),v⟩ dμ(x) = −∫_E u(x)(dφ(x)[v] − φ(x)dW(x)[v]) dμ(x). The displayed values of u and G use measurable representatives of their almost-everywhere equivalence classes. The closure is the single-valued partial linear extension whose graph is the topological closure of graph(D) in L²(μ; ℝ) × L²(μ; E); equivalently, the hypothesis on (u,G) means that graph pairs converge to it in both L² norms. No additional limit, regularity, or identification of the entire closure domain is asserted.
